solutions.latex:
Total perimeter $=3+3+\left(3\times\dfrac43\right)=10$ cm.

Hence for the second pendant:

$$10=2.5+2.5+2.5\times\theta\ \Rightarrow\ \theta=2\text{ radians}$$

$f(x)=x^3-3x^2$, $f'(x)=3x^2-6x$, $f''(x)=6x-6$.

Stationary points when $f'(x)=0$: $3x^2-6x=0$, $3x(x-2)=0$, so $x=0$ or $x=2$.

When $x=0$: $f(0)=0$, $f''(0)=-6<0$, so a maximum turning point at $(0,0)$.

When $x=2$: $f(2)=2^3-3\times4=-4$, $f''(2)=6\times2-6=6>0$, so a minimum turning point at $(2,-4)$.

$f(x)$ is concave up when $f''(x)>0$: $6x-6>0$, $6x>6$, $x>1$.

So $f(x)$ is concave up when $x>1$.

$y=x^2\log_e x$. Using the product rule, $y'=uv'+vu'$:

$$y'=x^2\cdot\dfrac1x+2x\cdot\log_e x=x+2x\ln x$$

$\dot x=8-8e^{-2t}$. Substituting $t=0$: $\dot x=8-8e^{-2(0)}=8-8=0$.

So the particle is initially at rest.
$\ddot x=16e^{-2t}$. As $e^{-2t}>0$ for all values of $t$, $\ddot x$ is always positive.
Since the particle is initially at rest (from a) and always has a positive acceleration (from b) for all $t>0$, it is moving in the positive direction.
$\dot x=8-8e^{-2t}$. As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-2t}\to0$, so $\dot x\to8$. The constant is $8$.

$$x^2+6x+y^2+2y=-6$$
$$x^2+6x+3^2+y^2+2y+1^2=-6+9+1$$
$$(x+3)^2+(y+1)^2=4$$

$10\sin^2x-4\sin x-5=0$. Using the quadratic formula:

$$\sin x=\dfrac{4\pm\sqrt{216}}{20}$$
$$\sin x\approx0.93485\ \text{or}\ -0.534847$$
$$x=69.2^\circ,\ 110.8^\circ\ \text{or}\ 212.3^\circ,\ 327.7^\circ$$

$V(x)=4x(8-x)^2$

$$V'(x)=4(x-8)^2+8x(x-8)=4(x-8)\left[(x-8)+2x\right]=4(x-8)(3x-8)$$

Stationary points: $V'(x)=0$ gives $x=8$ or $x=\dfrac83$.

$V''(x)=24x-128$.

When $x=8$: $V''(8)=24(8)-128>0$, minimum turning point.

When $x=\dfrac83$: $V''\left(\dfrac83\right)=24\left(\dfrac83\right)-128<0$, maximum turning point.

The maximum volume when $x=\dfrac83$ is

$$V\left(\dfrac83\right)=4\times\dfrac83\left(\dfrac83-8\right)^2=330\dfrac{11}{27}\ \text{cm}^3$$

Shaded area = area of the quarter circle less the area below the parabola between $x=0$ and $x=1$.

Area of $\dfrac14$ circle $=\dfrac14\pi r^2=\dfrac14\pi(2)^2=\pi$ sq units.

Area under the parabola between $x=0$ and $x=1$:

$$\int_0^1y\,dx=\int_0^1(x^2-3x+2)\,dx=\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}-\dfrac{3x^2}{2}+2x\right]_0^1=\left(\dfrac13-\dfrac32+2\right)-0=\dfrac56$$

$$\therefore\ \text{Shaded area}=\left(\pi-\dfrac56\right)\text{u}^2$$

This is an arithmetic sequence with first term $1$ and common difference $7$. Let the number of terms be $n$, so $S_n=396$.

$$\dfrac n2\left(2+7(n-1)\right)=396$$
$$n(7n-5)=792$$
$$7n^2-5n-792=0$$
$$(7n+72)(n-11)=0$$

$\Rightarrow n=11$ (since $-\dfrac{72}{7}$ is not an integer). The number of terms is $11$.

At 5 o'clock the angle $AOB=\dfrac5{12}\times360^\circ=150^\circ$.

Using the cosine rule:

$$x^2=10^2+7^2-2\times10\times7\times\cos150^\circ=270.243$$
$$x\approx\sqrt{270.243}\approx16.439$$
$$x\approx16.4\text{ cm (correct to 1 d.p.)}$$

$y=x^2-1$, $y'=2x$. At $x=a$, $y'=2a$.

Equation of the line with gradient $2a$ through $(a,a^2-1)$:

$$y-(a^2-1)=2a(x-a)$$
$$y-a^2+1=2ax-2a^2$$
$$y=2ax-a^2-1$$

If the tangent passes through $(3,-8)$:

$$2a(3)-a^2-1=-8$$
$$6a-a^2-1=-8$$
$$a^2-6a-7=0$$
$$(a-7)(a+1)=0\ \Rightarrow\ a=7\ \text{or}\ a=-1$$

Equations of tangents: $y=14x-50$ and $y=-2x-2$.
